## Motivation [Wan2.2 ModelSlim W4A4F4 checkpoints](https://modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers-MXFP-W4A4F4-DAOS) need packed FP4 weights, exported calibration data, and matching attention and precision paths to run in SGLang. This PR adds offline inference support on Ascend 950. ## Modifications - Repack ModelSlim exports into Diffusers checkpoints, preserving quantization descriptors, smoothing scales, and Q/K rotations while packing FP4 weights. - Support offline MXFP4/MXFP8 linears and timestep-based W4A4/W4A8 selection. Single-level MXFP4 weights remain ND; the existing dual-scale path retains its NZ requirement. - Run descriptor-selected MXFP4 self-attention with exported Q/K rotations through the experimental CANN `quant_flash_attn` extension. Real sequence lengths exclude padding from softmax. This path requires noncausal self-attention with head size 128 and no ring parallelism. - Invalidate legacy Cache-DiT residual and calibrator histories when effective precision changes, forcing computation for both CFG branches. For the default 40-step schedule, this protects W4A8 → W4A4 at global step 2 and W4A4 → W4A8 at step 38; the final two steps also compute fully. Explicit checkpoint-policy transitions are detected automatically. - Use token sharding for incompatible latent frame counts when allowed, reject an explicit sharding disable for those shapes, and use synchronous NPU-to-CPU component offload to avoid pinned-memory allocation failures. ## Accuracy Tests
Generate command ``` sglang generate --model-path "./Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers-MXFP-W4A4F4-DAOS/" --ulysses-degree 4 --num-gpus 4 --port 30088 --warmup-mode request --prompt "A cute happy Corgi playing in park sunset animated style" --seed 42 --num-frames 81 --num-inference-steps 40 --height 720 --width 1280 --dit-cpu-offload false --pin-cpu-memory false --quality high --enable-cache-dit true ```

 ```bash
   --save-output
 ```
 
-The offline MXFP4 checkpoint stores weights in an FP8 container and includes dual-level
-scales (`weight_scale`, `weight_dual_scale`). If exported with smooth quantization,
-`mul_scale` is loaded and applied before activation quantization to keep activations
-aligned with the calibrated weights.
+The repacker accepts numeric FP8 containers or packed `uint8` weights and produces
+packed FP4 `[out, in/2]` with `weight_scale` `[out, in/32]`. Dual-scale layers also
+require `weight_dual_scale` `[out, in/512, 1]`. Single-level weights use ND layout;
+dual-scale weights require NZ. Each TP input partition must be divisible by 64 or
+512, respectively. Both `div.mul_scale` and `mul_scale` descriptors are accepted:
+single-level layers apply smoothing once before quantization; dual-scale layers
+pass it as `smooth_scale` to the quantization operator.
+
+Existing ModelSlim diffusion checkpoints with numeric FP8 containers `[out, in]`
+also load directly: the loader packs their FP4 values before dtype conversion and
+tensor-parallel slicing. Already-packed FP4 bytes and genuine MXFP8 weights retain
+their existing loading paths.
+
+Single-level layers follow MindIE-SD's schedule: W4A8 for the first two and last two
+denoising steps, and W4A4 otherwise. A 40-step run uses W4A8 at zero-based indices
+0, 1, 38, and 39 to retain higher activation precision at the ends of denoising.
+Checkpoint entries in `timestep_policy.w4a4_linear` override this schedule; set
+`{"default": "W4A4"}` there for W4A4 throughout. Dual-scale layers stay W4A4 and
+reject W4A8 switching.
+
+### MXFP4 attention
+
+Self-attention blocks whose description selects `MXFP4_DYNAMIC` run quantized
+attention on Ascend 950PR/DT: Q/K/V are dynamically quantized to packed FP4 and
+evaluated by the CANN experimental `quant_flash_attn` extension. The exported
+Q/K rotation matrices (`to_q_rot`/`to_k_rot`, or `q_rot`/`k_rot` in earlier
+exports) are registered by the attention blocks and applied on quantized steps.
+
+- Sequences are padded to a kernel-friendly length (256 or 512, from
+  `mxfp4_attention_pad_size`); the real lengths are passed to the kernel so
+  padded positions never enter the softmax.
+- Packed (varlen) inputs are supported: sequences are bucketed by padded
+  length and evaluated per bucket, which is the path varlen models such as
+  MiniMax-H3 use.
+- `timestep_policy.fa` can switch attention between `FLOAT` (unquantized) and
+  `MXFP4` per step.
+- FP8 attention descriptors (`FP8_DYNAMIC`) are rejected: FP8 attention
+  requires custom MindIE kernels that SGLang does not ship. Re-quantize such
+  checkpoints with MXFP4 attention or keep attention in BF16.
+
+### Linear backward compatibility
+
+Every single-level MXFP4 path uses MindIE-SD's activation-quantization defaults
+(`round_mode="rint"`, `scale_alg=2`, `dst_type_max=7.25`); checkpoint
+`mxfp4_scale_alg`/`mxfp4_dst_type_max` descriptors override the two kwargs.
+Only the W4A8 boundary steps keep operator-default rounding — their activation
+destination is FP8, to which the FP4-targeted kwargs do not apply.
+
+| Linear path | Weight layout | Activation rounding | Matmul bias |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Offline single-level W4A4 (SRT and diffusion) | ND | `rint` + C7 kwargs | FP32, original shape |
+| Offline single-level W4A8 boundary steps (SRT and diffusion) | FP4-aware NZ (SRT) / same ND weights (diffusion) | Operator default (FP8 destination) | FP32, original shape (SRT) / BF16 `[1, out]` (diffusion) |
+| MXFP4 attention (Q/K/V) | — | `rint` + C7 kwargs | — |
+
+SRT online `--quantization mxfp4` and diffusion online `--quantization mxfp4_npu`
+retain their separate dual-level paths (operator-default arguments; the
+dual-level operator's support for these kwargs must be verified on device).
+CPU checks can verify dispatch and operator arguments; numerical accuracy,
+video quality, and performance require target-NPU validation.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Cache-DiT precision guard for timestep-quantized diffusion transformers."""
+
+from functools import wraps
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def set_quant_precision_guard(transformer):
+    """Clear both CFG histories and force computation when quant precision changes."""
+    modules = getattr(transformer, "modules", None)
+    if modules is None:
+        return
+    attention_policies = []
+    policies = []
+    for module in modules():
+        if getattr(module, "use_mxfp4_attention", False):
+            attention_policies.append(module.attention_quant_description)
+        scheme = getattr(module, "scheme", None)
+        target = getattr(scheme, "precision_policy_target", None)
+        if target is not None and not any(scheme is p for p in policies):
+            policies.append(scheme)
+    if not (attention_policies or policies) or getattr(
+        transformer.forward, "_sglang_precision_guard", False
+    ):
+        return
+
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.quantization.mxfp4_utils import (
+        default_mxfp4_policy,
+        resolve_precision,
+    )
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.forward_context import (
+        get_forward_context_or_none,
+    )
+
+    original_forward = transformer.forward
+    previous_signature = previous_batch = previous_step = force_step = None
+
+    @wraps(original_forward)
+    def guarded_forward(*args, **kwargs):
+        nonlocal previous_signature, previous_batch, previous_step, force_step
+        context = get_forward_context_or_none()
+        if context is None:
+            return original_forward(*args, **kwargs)
+        batch, step = context.forward_batch, context.current_timestep
+        num_steps = getattr(batch, "num_inference_steps", 0)
+        if batch is not previous_batch or (
+            previous_step is not None and step < previous_step
+        ):
+            previous_signature = force_step = None
+        default_policy = default_mxfp4_policy(num_steps)
+        signature = tuple(
+            resolve_precision(description, "fa", "MXFP4", default_policy)
+            for description in attention_policies
+        ) + tuple(scheme.resolve_precision(default_policy) for scheme in policies)
+        contexts = [
+            transformer._context_manager.get_context(name)
+            for name in transformer._context_names
+        ]
+        changed = previous_signature is not None and signature != previous_signature
+        if previous_signature is None or changed:
+            # Drop both CFG histories without restarting the expert's local step counter.
+            for cached_context in contexts:
+                cached_context.clear_buffers()
+                for calibrator in (
+                    *cached_context.get_calibrators(),
+                    *cached_context.get_cfg_calibrators(),
+                ):
+                    if calibrator is not None:
+                        calibrator.reset_cache()
+            force_step = step
+            if changed:
+                logger.info(
+                    "step=%d quant precision changed; invalidating cached residuals",
+                    step,
+                )
+        previous_signature, previous_batch, previous_step = signature, batch, step
+        force = (
+            step == force_step or step < 2 or (num_steps > 0 and step >= num_steps - 2)
+        )
+        masks = [c.cache_config.steps_computation_mask for c in contexts]
+        if force:
+            for cached_context in contexts:
+                # SCM takes precedence over similarity, including static reuse policies.
+                cached_context.cache_config.steps_computation_mask = [1] * max(
+                    num_steps, cached_context.executed_steps + 1
+                )
+        try:
+            return original_forward(*args, **kwargs)
+        finally:
+            for cached_context, mask in zip(contexts, masks):
+                cached_context.cache_config.steps_computation_mask = mask
+
+    guarded_forward._sglang_precision_guard = True
+    transformer.forward = guarded_forward
